name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deeply Republican district with a -23 point partisan lean
Incumbent Rick Crawford running for reelection with a large financial advantage
Democrat Terri Green has raised only about $65,000 with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 96 percent
model.rationale: Crawford holds a seat whose fundamentals favor Republicans by more than twenty points, is a well-funded incumbent, and faces a challenger who has raised almost nothing; markets and the fundamentals both point to an easy Republican win. Nothing in the available evidence suggests movement toward the Democrat.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending push or a dramatic statewide political shift in Arkansas would be needed to put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rick Crawford is seeking another term in a northeastern Arkansas district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan baseline of roughly twenty-three points in the GOP's favor. He enters the general election with about $1 million on hand after raising more than $940,000, while Democrat Terri Green has raised about $65,000 and holds under $12,000, leaving her little capacity to introduce herself to voters. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign activity.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the funding gap, and prediction markets, which give the Republican roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. The expected margin is around twenty points Republican, with the Democrat needing an extraordinary, unforeseen shift to compete.
